    ```sysml
    // Features and design options.
    //
    // A design option is native SysML: a `variation` (a definition or a usage whose
    // body holds only `variant` members; SysML-textual-bnf.kebnf:224 for the definition
    // prefix, :282 for the usage prefix, :254-256 the variant member). MEMO adds
    // nothing to how one is written. What SysML has no word for is WHY a variant exists
    // and WHICH ones go together: that is a product feature.
    //
    //   part featEuMarket : ProductFeature;                    // the market EU releases target
    //   variation part energyOutput : LogicalComponent {
    //       variant part euOutput : LogicalComponent;          // a variant, for the EU
    //       variant part usOutput : LogicalComponent;
    //   }
    //   #RealizesFeature dependency from energyOutput::euOutput to featEuMarket;
    //   connection : RequiresFeature connect ...               // one feature needs another
    //
    // A release selects features (`#SelectsFeature`), and through them the variants it
    // contains; a rule counts one variant per variation point from that. A feature is
    // a usage like any other part, named by the family, and a platform package may
    // declare the family's features once.
    //
    // A variation point cannot own attributes: SysIDE rejects an owned feature in a
    // variation (`usage-variation-owned-feature-membership`). Identity metadata is an
    // annotation and is allowed (measured on E0, 2026-10-13); `status` and anything else
    // a variation point would carry goes on its variants.
    package memo_architecture_variability {
        private import Metaobjects::SemanticMetadata;
        private import ScalarValues::*;

        private import memo_core_common::*;
        private import memo_core_enumerations::*;
        private import memo_core_relationships::*;

        // Named ProductFeature, not Feature: `Feature` is the KerML metaclass, and the
        // builder falls back to a metaclass name for a kind it cannot place.
        part def ProductFeature specializes MemoPart;

        // `Requires` is taken by the native `require` relation, so these say what they join.
        connection def RequiresFeature :> MemoRelationship {
            doc /* Selecting the source feature needs the target feature selected too. */
            end dependentFeature : ProductFeature :>> source;
            end requiredFeature : ProductFeature :>> target;
        }
        abstract connection requiresFeatureLinks : RequiresFeature[*];
        metadata def <requiresFeature> RequiresFeatureMetadata :> SemanticMetadata {
            :> annotatedElement : SysML::ConnectionDefinition;
            :> annotatedElement : SysML::ConnectionUsage;
            :>> baseType = requiresFeatureLinks meta SysML::Usage;
        }

        connection def ExcludesFeature :> MemoRelationship {
            doc /* The two features cannot be selected together. Symmetric: either end may be written first. */
            end firstFeature : ProductFeature :>> source;
            end secondFeature : ProductFeature :>> target;
        }
        abstract connection excludesFeatureLinks : ExcludesFeature[*];
        metadata def <excludesFeature> ExcludesFeatureMetadata :> SemanticMetadata {
            :> annotatedElement : SysML::ConnectionDefinition;
            :> annotatedElement : SysML::ConnectionUsage;
            :>> baseType = excludesFeatureLinks meta SysML::Usage;
        }

        // Typed dependencies (memo_core_relationships::MemoTypedDependency): the variant
        // is nested in its variation, so it is a dependency's client by qualified name.
        metadata def RealizesFeature :> MemoTypedDependency {
            doc /* `#RealizesFeature dependency from <variant> to <feature>;` The variant exists to give the family this feature. */
        }
        metadata def SelectsFeature :> MemoTypedDependency {
            doc /* `#SelectsFeature dependency from <release> to <feature>, <feature>;` The release contains the variants that realize these features. */
        }
    }

    ```
